# Desktop emulator

`tools/emu/` compiles the real `TamaPoke.ino`, `pet.cpp`, `battle.cpp`, `i18n.cpp`, `species_chirp.cpp` and `thumb_format.cpp` unmodified and replaces only the hardware (display canvas, touch, NVS, SD, RTC, PMU, audio, IMU). What you see is the real 466×466 RGB565 framebuffer. It is a UI/logic tool, not a substitute for the board: timing, DMA, PSRAM pressure, audio, battery and real touch only exist on hardware.

Originally from DylanPDao/TamaPoke (MIT), reworked for this firmware. Its README: `tools/emu/README.md`.

## Setup

- `make emu-build` needs `g++`, `python3` and SDL2. If `sdl2-config` exists it is used; otherwise run `make emu-setup` once: it unpacks SDL2 into `tools/emu/.sdl` without root (Debian/Ubuntu, uses `apt-get download`). Installing `libsdl2-dev` with sudo also works.
- The window works on WSL2 through WSLg (`DISPLAY=:0`).
- Sprites are read from `tools/sdcard/mons/` (generated by `tools/pack_pmd.py`). Without them the firmware runs its no-sprites path.

## Running

| Command | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `make emu` | build and open the window (real time) |
| `make emu-fast` | same at 60× time (1 game minute = 1 real second) |
| `make emu FAST=300 SAVE=.dev/tmp/x.nvs` | any speed, separate save file |
| `tools/emu/tamapoke-emu --wipe` | start with a fresh save (the pet is stored in the `--save` file, default `tamapoke.nvs` in the current directory) |

In the window: click = touch, drag = swipe, hold `W` = walk (≈2 steps/s, independent of `--fast`), `S` = shake, `Esc` = quit and save. The time scale is suspended while you touch the panel, because gestures are timed on the same clock (a tap needs under 1.5 s).

Type serial commands in the terminal that started the emulator: `STATS`, `HEALTH`, `TIME`, `STEPS`, `IMU`, `SHAKE`, `WIPE` and others from the sketch's serial handler. Debug-only commands (`TESTMON`, `TESTEVO`, ...) work because the emulator builds with `TAMAPOKE_LOCAL_TEST`.

## Headless screenshots (for agents)

An agent cannot see the window. Use `make emu-shot` instead: it runs the firmware without a window, optionally performs taps, then writes a PPM.

```bash
make emu-shot TAPS="233,145" MS=2000          # tap once, wait 2 s, capture
make emu-shot FAST=60 MS=600000               # 10 game minutes later
python3 -c "from PIL import Image; Image.open('.dev/tmp/shot.ppm').save('.dev/tmp/shot.png')"
```

Then view `.dev/tmp/shot.png`. `MS` is game time (scaled by `FAST`). Each tap presses 120 ms, releases and settles 600 ms; taps run after a 1 s boot. Delete `.dev/tmp` files afterwards. The first screen on a fresh save is "Choose your starter" (Kanto/Johto/Hoenn at y≈145/222/300), then the starter choice.

## Troubleshooting

- `libsamplerate.so.0`/`libdecor` not found at start: rerun `make emu-setup` (the rootless copy includes both) and rebuild; the binary uses an rpath into `tools/emu/.sdl`.
- Compile error about a missing Arduino/ESP32 symbol after a firmware change: add a stub to `tools/emu/Arduino.h` (core API), `tools/emu/Arduino_GFX_Library.h` (display) or `tools/emu/host_impl.cpp` (SD, RTC, PMU, audio, IMU).
- A new sketch function used before its definition: `genproto.py` regenerates `proto.h` on every build; it skips `static` functions.
- Everything under `tools/emu/` besides sources is generated and gitignored (`.sdl/`, `tamapoke-emu`, `proto.h`, `sketch.cpp`, `*.nvs`).
